 Let's calculate step-by-step:

\n\n
    \n\t
  • Mean of combined group: \\( \\mu_{combined} = \\frac{50 \\times 63 + 40 \\times 54}{50 + 40} = 59 \\)
    • \n\t
  • Variance of male workers: \\( \\sigma_1^2 = 9^2 = 81 \\)
    • \n\t
  • Variance of female workers: \\( \\sigma_2^2 = 6^2 = 36 \\)
    • \n\t
  • Combined variance: \\( \\sigma_{combined}^2 = \\frac{49 \\times 81 + 39 \\times 36 + 50 \\times (63 - 59)^2 + 40 \\times (54 - 59)^2}{89} \\)
    • \n\t
  • Combined standard deviation: \\( \\sigma_{combined} = \\sqrt{81} = 9 \\)
    • \n
\n\n

Hence, the standard deviation of the combined group of 90 workers is 9.

          • The limits of a multiple correlation coefficient R1.23 are 0 ≤ R1.23 ≤ 1:\n\n\t
              \n\t\t
            • The multiple correlation coefficient (R) measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between one dependent variable and two or more independent variables.
              • \n\t\t
            • The value of R ranges from 0 to 1. An R value of 0 indicates no linear relationship, while an R value of 1 indicates a perfect linear relationship.
              • \n\t\t
            • In the context of a financial enterprise, understanding the strength of the relationship between financial variables can help in making more informed decisions. For example, R1.23 could measure the relationship between a company's revenue (dependent variable) and two independent variables such as marketing spend and economic conditions.

              Key Points

              \n\n
                \n\t
              • Increasing (1 - α) increases the width of the confidence interval of the mean:\n\n\t
                  \n\t\t
                • The confidence interval represents the range within which the true population parameter is expected to lie, given a certain level of confidence (1 - α).
                  • \n\t\t
                • When (1 - α) increases, it means we are increasing our confidence level, for example, from 95% to 99%.
                  • \n\t\t
                • To accommodate this higher confidence level, the confidence interval must widen to ensure that the true population parameter is captured within this interval more often.
                  • \n\t\t
                • In a financial enterprise, this means we can be more certain about the average values of financial metrics but at the cost of a broader range, which might affect precision in decision-making.

                \n\t
                • \n

                  • \n\t
                \n\t
                • \n\t
              • Is reduced by half:\n\t
                  \n\t\t

                        \n\n
                          \n\t
                        • Empirical probability is calculated based on the number of favorable outcomes divided by the total number of trials.
                          • \n\t
                        • Here, the die is thrown four times, so the total number of trials is 4.
                          • \n\t
                        • The number of times 5 is obtained is 2.
                          • \n\t
                        • Therefore, the empirical probability of getting a 5 is calculated as 2/4 = 0.5.

                        • Option 4 (0.8): This value suggests an even higher frequency of 5, which is incorrect.
                          • \n
                        \n\n

                                        \n\n
                                          \n\t
                                        • Definition: The Poisson distribution is a discrete probability distribution that expresses the probability of a given number of events occurring in a fixed interval of time or space.
                                          • \n\t
                                        • Parameter (λ): For a Poisson distribution, the parameter λ (lambda) represents both the mean and the variance.
                                          • \n\t
                                        • Given: In this case, the parameter λ is given as 5.
                                          • \n\t
                                        • Variance: The variance of a Poisson-distributed random variable X with parameter λ is also λ.
                                          • \n\t
                                        • Conclusion: Therefore, the variance of X is 5.

                                        \n\n

                                        Important Points

                                        \n\n

                                        \n\n
                                          \n\t
                                        • Option 1 (3): The variance of a Poisson distribution is equal to its parameter λ. Since λ is 5, variance cannot be 3.

                                          • \n\t
                                        • Option 3 (2): Again, this does not match the given parameter λ, which is 5.
                                          • \n\t
                                        • Option 5 (Blank): This option is not valid and does not provide any answer.
                                          • \n
                                        \n\n

                                        Hence, for a random variable X following a Poisson distribution with parameter 5, the variance of X is indeed 5.

                                            • In a financial enterprise context, having a high power in tests such as credit risk assessment", "te": "", "mr": "", "bn": "", "ml": "", "gu": "", "kn": "", "ta": "", "or": "", "as": "", "ks": "", "kok": "", "mni": "", "ne": "", "pa": "", "sd": "", "ur": "", "sat": "", "mai": "", "brx": "", "doi": "", "sa": "", "grt": "", "kha": "", "lus": "", "bo": "", "trp": ""}, "tags": [], "concept": "Unidentified", "confidence": "unidentified"}, {"qid": "654120d83110f00ac742fee4", "qs_no": 21, "pos_marks": 2.0, "neg_marks": 0.5, "type": "mcq", "langs": {"en": {"value": "The power of a test is: ", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "P(Type I error )&nbsp;"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "1 - P(Type II error )&nbsp;"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "P(Type II error )&nbsp;"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "1 - P(Type I error )&nbsp;&nbsp;"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}, "hn": {"value": "किसी परीक्षण की शक्ति होती है:", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "P(प्रकार I त्रुटि)"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "1 - P(प्रकार II त्रुटि)"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "P(प्रकार II त्रुटि)"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "1 - P(प्रकार I त्रुटि)"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "2", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

                                              The power of a test is 1 - P(Type II error).

                                              \n\n

                                              Key Points

                                              \n\n
                                                \n\t
                                              • 1 - P(Type II error):\n\n\t
                                                  \n\t\t
                                                • The power of a test is defined as the probability that the test correctly rejects the null hypothesis when the alternative hypothesis is true. It is calculated as 1 minus the probability of a Type II error (β).
                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                • In a financial enterprise context, having a high power in tests such as credit risk assessments or fraud detection means accurately identifying true positives, thereby minimizing potential financial losses.
                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                • Improving the power of a test can involve increasing the sample size, choosing more effective test statistics, or improving data quality.
                                                  • \n\t
                                                \n\t
                                                • \n
                                              \n\n

                                              Additional Information

                                              \n\n
                                                \n\t
                                              • P(Type I error):\n\n\t
                                                  \n\t\t
                                                • This is the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true, also known as the significance level (α). While important in hypothesis testing, it does not define the power of a test.
                                                  • \n\t
                                                \n\t
                                                • \n\t
                                              • P(Type II error):\n\t
                                                  \n\t\t
                                                • This is the probability of failing to reject the null hypothesis when the alternative hypothesis is true. It is denoted by β. The power of a test is inversely related to this probability but not equal to it.
                                                  • \n\t
                                                \n\t
                                                • \n\t
                                              • 1 - P(Type I error):\n\t
                                                  \n\t\t
                                                • This represents the probability of not making a Type I error, but it does not relate to the power of the test. It is more about the test's ability to avoid false positives.
                                                  • \n\t
                                                \n\t
                                                • \n
                                              ", "hn": "\n

                                              किसी परीक्षण की शक्ति 1 - P(प्रकार II त्रुटि) होती है।Key Points

                                                \n\t

                                                      • Stratified random sampling:\n\n\t
                                                          \n\t\t
                                                        • In stratified random sampling, the population is divided into distinct subgroups or strata, and random samples are taken from each stratum. This technique ensures representation from all subgroups, making it a probability sampling method.
                                                          • \n\t
                                                        \n\t
                                                        • \n\t
                                                      • Simple random sampling:\n\t
                                                          \n\t\t
                                                        • Simple random sampling involves selecting subjects from the population in such a way that every member has an equal chance of being chosen. This technique is the most straightforward form of probability sampling.
                                                          • \n\t
                                                        \n\t
                                                        • \n\t
                                                      • Systematic sampling:\n\t
                                                          \n\t\t
                                                        • Systematic sampling involves selecting every nth member of the population after a random start. This method ensures a degree of randomness and is considered a probability sampling technique.

                                                      The correct answer is F test

                                                      \n\n

                                                      Key Points One Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA):

                                                      \n\n
                                                        \n\t
                                                      • F test is used in a one way analysis of variance to compare the variances between groups.
                                                        • \n\t
                                                      • It helps in determining if there are any statistically significant differences between the means of three or more independent groups.
                                                        • \n\t
                                                      • The F statistic is calculated as the ratio of the variance between the group means to the variance within the groups.
                                                        • \n\t
                                                      • A larger F value indicates a greater degree of difference between the group means.
                                                        • \n

                                                          The correct answer is 168

                                                          \n\n

                                                          Key Points Moments of Distribution:

                                                          \n\n
                                                            \n\t
                                                          • The nth moment of a distribution about a value 'a' is given by E[(X−a)n]E[(X−a)n]\n\t\n\t.
                                                            • \n\t
                                                          • The nth moment about zero is given by E[Xn]E[Xn]\n\t\n\t.
                                                            • \n\t
                                                          • The relationship between moments about any value and moments about zero involves binomial expansion.
                                                            • \n\t
                                                          • Given the moments about the value 2, we can calculate the moments about zero using binomial expansion.
                                                            • \n
                                                          \n\n

                                                          Important Calculation

                                                          \n\n

                                                           Given moments about 2: M′1=1M1′=1\n\n, M′2=2.5M2′=2.5\n\n, M′3=5.5M3′=5.5\n\n, M′4=16M4′=16\n\n.

                                                          \n\n

                                                          Using the binomial theorem:

                                                          \n\n

                                                          Fourth moment about zero:

                                                          \n\n

                                                          \\(M_4 = M'_4 + 4 \\cdot 2 \\cdot M'_3 + 6 \\cdot 2^2 \\cdot M'_2 + 4 \\cdot 2^3 \\cdot M'_1 + 2^4\\)

                                                          \n\n

                                                          \\(M_4 = 16 + 4 \\cdot 2 \\cdot 5.5 + 6 \\cdot 4 \\cdot 2.5 + 4 \\cdot 8 \\cdot 1 + 16\\)

                                                          \n\n

                                                          \\(M_4 = 16 + 44 + 60 + 32 + 16\\)

                                                          \n\n

                                                          \\(M_4 = 168\\)

                                                          \n\n

                                                          Therefore, the fourth moment about zero is 168.

                                                              • \n\t

                                                                        निम्नलिखित एक यादृच्छिक मूल 5 से दिए गए परिघात हैं।

                                                                        \n", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "32"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "48"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "19"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "6"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "3", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

                                                                        The correct answer is 19

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        Key Points Moments About an Arbitrary Origin:

                                                                        \n\n
                                                                          \n\t
                                                                        • Moments are statistical measures that describe the shape of a set of points. They are used to understand the distribution and other characteristics of the data.
                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                        • The first moment (μ1’) is the mean of the data.
                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                        • The second moment (μ2’) is related to the variance, which measures the spread of the data.
                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                        • The third moment (μ3’) is related to the skewness, which measures the asymmetry of the data distribution.
                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                        • The fourth moment (μ4’) is related to the kurtosis, which measures the "tailedness" of the data distribution.
                                                                          • \n
                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        Important Points

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                         Given the moments about an arbitrary origin, we can calculate the central moments using the relationship between raw moments and central moments.

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        Given:

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        μ1' = -4

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        μ2' = 22

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        μ3' = -117

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        μ4' = 560

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        To find μ3:

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        \\(μ3 = μ3' - 3μ2'μ1' + 2μ1'^3\\)

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        Substitute the values:

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        \\(μ3 = -117 - 3(22)(-4) + 2(-4)^3\\)

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        \\(μ3 = -117 + 264 - 128\\)

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        \\(μ3 = 264 - 245 = 19\\)

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        \\(μ3 = 19\\)

                                                                        \n\n

                                                                        Therefore, the correct answer is 19.

                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                      • A function f(x) is a probability mass function (PMF) if the sum of f(x) over all possible values of x equals 1.
                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                      • In this case, the given function is a binomial probability mass function: f(x)=n!x!(n−x)!kx(1−k)n−xf(x)=n!x!(n−x)!kx(1−k)n−x\n\t\n\t.
                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                      • The sum of all binomial probabilities for a given n is always 1, provided k is the probability of success (0 ≤ k ≤ 1).
                                                                                        • \n\t

                                                                                          \n\n
                                                                                            \n\t
                                                                                          • Paasche's index is a price index that uses the current period quantities as weights.
                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                          • It measures the relative change in the price level of a basket of goods and services in the current period compared to the base period.
                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                          • The formula is given by Σp1q1Σp0q1.100Σp1q1Σp0q1.100Σp1q1Σp0q1.100\n\t\n\t , where p1p1p1\n\t\n\t and p0p0p0\n\t\n\t are the prices in the current and base periods, respectively, and q1q1q1\n\t\n\t is the quantity in the current period.
                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                          • This index number reflects the cost of purchasing the current period's basket of goods at current prices relative to base period prices.
                                                                                            • \n

                                                                                              The correct answer is r(X,Y) = \\(\\frac{Cov(X,Y)}{\\sigma_X \\sigma_Y }\\)

                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                              Key Points Correlation Coefficient:

                                                                                              \n\n
                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                              • r(X,Y) = \\(\\frac{Cov(X,Y)}{\\sigma_X \\sigma_Y }\\) is the correct formula for the correlation coefficient.
                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                              • It standardizes the covariance by dividing it by the product of the standard deviations of X and Y.
                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                              • This formula ensures that the correlation coefficient lies between -1 and 1.
                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                              • It measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two variables.
                                                                                                • \n
                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                              Important Points

                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                               Explanation of Incorrect Options:

                                                                                              \n\n
                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                              • Option 1: r(X, Y) = Cov(X, Y) - σX σY\n\n\t
                                                                                                  \n\t\t
                                                                                                • This option incorrectly subtracts the product of the standard deviations from the covariance.
                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                • It does not provide a standardized measure of correlation.
                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                • The result can fall outside the range of -1 to 1.
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                              • Option 2: r(X, Y) = Cov(X, Y) + σX σY\n\t
                                                                                                  \n\t\t
                                                                                                • This option incorrectly adds the product of the standard deviations to the covariance.
                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                • It also fails to standardize the covariance.
                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                • This formula can yield values outside the acceptable range for correlation coefficients.
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                              • Option 4: r(X, Y) = \\(\\frac{\\sigma_X\\sigma_Y}{Cov(X,Y)}\\)\n\t
                                                                                                  \n\t\t
                                                                                                • This option incorrectly inverts the relationship by dividing the product of the standard deviations by the covariance.
                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                • It does not provide a meaningful measure of correlation.
                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                • The values obtained from this formula are not constrained between -1 and 1.
                                                                                                  • \n\t

                                                                                              Key Points

                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                               To find the probability that the disease was diagnosed correctly given that the patient died, we use Bayes' theorem:

                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                              Let:

                                                                                              \n\n
                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                              • D: Disease is diagnosed correctly.
                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                              • D': Disease is diagnosed incorrectly.
                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                              • Die: Patient dies.
                                                                                                • \n
                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                              We need to find P(D | Die).

                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                              \\(P(D | Die) = \\frac{P(Die | D) \\cdot P(D)}{P(Die)}\\)

                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                              The correct answer is 6/13.

                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                              Key Points

                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                               To find the probability that the disease was diagnosed correctly given that the patient died, we use Bayes' theorem:

                                                                                                • \n\tसही उत्तर 6/13 है।Key Points

                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                यह जानने के लिए कि रोगी की मृत्यु के बाद बीमारी का सही निदान होने की प्रायिकता क्या है, हम बेयस प्रमेय का उपयोग करते हैं:

                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                मान लीजिए:

                                                                                                \n\n
                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                • D: बीमारी का सही निदान किया गया है।
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                • D': बीमारी का गलत निदान किया गया है।
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                • मृत्यु: रोगी की मृत्यु हो जाती है।
                                                                                                  • \n
                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                हमें P(D | मृत्यु) ज्ञात करने की आवश्यकता है।

                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                \\(P(D | Die) = \\frac{P(Die | D) \\cdot P(D)}{P(Die)}\\)

                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                जहां:

                                                                                                \n\n
                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                • \\(P(D) = 0.6\\)
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                • \\(P(D') = 0.4\\)
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                • \\(P(Die | D) = 0.4\\)
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                • \\(P(Die | D') = 0.7\\)
                                                                                                  • \n
                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                कुल प्रायिकता के नियम का उपयोग करके:

                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                \\(P(Die) = P(Die | D) \\cdot P(D) + P(Die | D') \\cdot P(D')\\)

                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                \\(P(Die) = 0.4 \\cdot 0.6 + 0.7 \\cdot 0.4 = 0.24 + 0.28 = 0.52\\)

                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                इसलिए,

                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                \\(P(D | Die) = \\frac{0.4 \\cdot 0.6}{0.52} = \\frac{0.24}{0.52} = \\frac{6}{13}\\)

                                                                                                \nदिए गए PDF का बहुलक ज्ञात करना:

                                                                                                \n\n
                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                • बहुलक की परिभाषा: एक प्रायिकता घनत्व फलन (pdf) का बहुलक x का वह मान होता है जिस पर pdf अपना अधिकतम मान प्राप्त करता है।
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                • दिए गए pdf का बहुलक ज्ञात करने के लिए, हमें x का वह मान ज्ञात करना होगा जो फलन f(x)=3(2x−x2)4f(x)=3(2x−x2)4 को 0≤x≤20≤x≤2 के लिए अधिकतम करता है।
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                • व्युत्पन्न दृष्टिकोण: हम x के सापेक्ष f(x)f(x) का व्युत्पन्न लेते हैं और इसे शून्य पर सेट करते हैं ताकि क्रांतिक बिंदु ज्ञात हो सकें।
                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                • f′(x)=0f′(x)=0 को हल करने पर, हमें क्रांतिक बिंदु x = 1 प्राप्त होता है।
                                                                                                  • \n\t

                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                          • The formula for the nth decile is D_n = (n/10) * (N+1), where N is the number of data points.
                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                          • Here, N = 8 and n = 8. So, D_8 = (8/10) * (8+1) = 7.2
                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                          • The 8th decile lies between the 7th and 8th data points in the sorted list, which are 32 and 36 respectively. Hence, the 8th decile is approximately 32.

                                                                                                              • Positively skewed distribution:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                  \n\t\t
                                                                                                                • In a positively skewed distribution, the tail on the right side (higher values) is longer or fatter than the left side (lower values).
                                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                • This occurs when there are a few exceptionally high values that pull the mean to the right, making the mean greater than the median, which in turn is greater than the mode.
                                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                • For a financial enterprise, this could indicate that while most data points (such as revenue or returns) are clustered at lower values, there are some significant outliers that are much higher, skewing the average.

                                                                                                                  Key Points

                                                                                                                  \n\n
                                                                                                                    \n\t
                                                                                                                  • Normalization Condition:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • The probability density function (PDF) of a continuous random variable must satisfy the condition that the total probability is 1.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • This means that the integral of the given function from 0 to 1 must be equal to 1.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    \n\t
                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                  • Given PDF Function:\n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • The PDF is given as f(x) = kx2 (1 - x3).
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • To determine the value of\\( ( k )\\), we set up the equation:
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • ∫[0 to 1] kx2 (1 - x3) dx = 1
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    \n\t
                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                  • Solving the Integral:\n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • Expanding the function inside the integral:
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • ∫[0 to 1] k(x2 - x5) dx = 1
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • Computing the individual integrals:
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • k [ (x3)/3 - (x6)/6 ] | from 0 to 1 = 1
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • Substituting the limits:
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • k (1/3 - 1/6) = 1
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • k (1/6) = 1
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • Solving for (k), we get k = 6 .
                                                                                                                      • \n\t

                                                                                                                  • Probability Density Function (PDF):\n\n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • A function that describes the likelihood of a random variable taking a particular value in a continuous range.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • The total area under the PDF curve must be equal to 1.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    \n\t
                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                  • Integral in Probability:\n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • In probability theory, integration is used to find the total probability over a continuous range.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • This is necessary for normalizing the function to satisfy probability properties.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    \n\t
                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                  • Importance of Normalization:\n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • Ensuring that the PDF integrates to 1 is crucial for correctly defining the distribution.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                    • Normalization helps in determining unknown constants in probability distributions.

                                                                                                                      \n\t
                                                                                                                    • Ratio-to-trend method:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                        \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • This method involves calculating the ratio of actual values to the trend values to measure seasonal variation.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • It helps in identifying how much the actual data deviates from the trend due to seasonal factors.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    • Simple averages:\n\t
                                                                                                                        \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • This method calculates the average of data for each season to measure seasonal variation.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • It is a straightforward approach that helps in understanding the typical seasonal pattern.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    • Ratio-to-moving-average method:\n\t
                                                                                                                        \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • This method involves dividing the actual data by the moving average to eliminate trend effects and isolate seasonal variations.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • It is a common quantitative technique used to measure seasonal fluctuations.

                                                                                                                    Key Points Explanation:

                                                                                                                    \n\n
                                                                                                                      \n\t
                                                                                                                    • Degrees of Freedom: The degrees of freedom (df) for a two-sample t-test is calculated as the sum of the sample sizes minus 2. In this case, df = (16 - 1) + (14 - 1) = 28.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    • The t-distribution is appropriate for comparing the means of two small samples.
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    • The test statistic value of 1.45 is derived from the formula for the t-test for independent samples.

                                                                                                                    \n\n

                                                                                                                    Key Points Explanation of Correct and Incorrect Options:

                                                                                                                    \n\n
                                                                                                                      \n\t
                                                                                                                    • Option 1: μ2 = μ2' + (μ1')2\n\n\t
                                                                                                                        \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • This option incorrectly adds the square of the first moment about the origin (μ1') to the second moment about the origin (μ2').
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • The correct relationship involves subtracting the square of the first moment about the origin.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • Hence, this option is incorrect.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t
                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                    • Option 2: μ2 = μ2'\n\t
                                                                                                                        \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • This option states that the second moment about the mean (μ2) is equal to the second moment about the origin (μ2').
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • However, this ignores the contribution of the first moment about the origin (μ1').
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • Therefore, this option is incorrect.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                      \n\t
                                                                                                                      • \n\t

                                                                                                                        • \n\t

                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t

                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • Hence, this option is correct.

                                                                                                                        \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • Seasonal variation refers to periodic fluctuations that occur at regular intervals due to seasonal factors, such as festivals, holidays, or weather changes.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • In the context of a departmental store, sales typically increase during festivals due to higher consumer spending driven by holiday shopping, special promotions, and cultural traditions.
                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                      • This pattern repeats annually, making it a clear example of seasonal variation in a time series.

They are often caused by unforeseen events such as natural disasters or political instability.

                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                  • This statement is true. When conditioning on the entire sample space S, the probability of event A given S is simply the probability of A, as S encompasses all possible outcomes.
                                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                • P(A|B) = P(B|A):\n\t
                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                  • This is the incorrect statement. In probability theory, P(A|B) and P(B|A) are generally not equal. P(A|B) is the probability of A occurring given that B has occurred, whereas P(B|A) is the probability of B occurring given that A has occurred. These two are not interchangeable.
                                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                • A and ϕ are independent:\n\t
                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                  • This statement is true. The empty set ϕ (which represents an impossible event) is independent of any event A because P(ϕ) = 0 and P(A ∩ ϕ) = 0, fulfilling the definition of independence (P(A ∩ ϕ) = P(A)P(ϕ)).
                                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                • A and S are independent:\n\t
                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                  • This statement is true. Any event A is independent of the entire sample space S because P(A ∩ S) = P(A) and P(S) = 1, thus P(A ∩ S) = P(A)P(S).
                                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                  • \n
                                                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                                                The correct answer is P(A|B) = P(B|A).

                                                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                                                Key Points

                                                                                                                                  \n\t

                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t

                                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                • A and ϕ are independent:\n\t
                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                  • This statement is true. The empty set ϕ (which represents an impossible event) is independent of any event A because P(ϕ) = 0 and P(A ∩ ϕ) = 0, fulfilling the definition of independence (P(A ∩ ϕ) = P(A)P(ϕ)).
                                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                  • \n\t

                                                                                                                                • Understanding Conditional Probability:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                  • Conditional probability P(A|B) represents the probability of event A occurring given that event B has occurred. It is calculated as P(A ∩ B) / P(B), provided that P(B) > 0.
                                                                                                                                    • \n\t
                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                • Independence of Events:\n\t
                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                  • Two events A and B are independent if and only if the occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the occurrence of the other, i.e., P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B).

                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t

                                                                                                                                    Key Points Variance and Data Transformation:

                                                                                                                                    \n\n
                                                                                                                                      \n\t
                                                                                                                                    • Variance measures the spread of a set of data points.
                                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                                    • When each observation in a data set is multiplied by a constant, the variance is multiplied by the square of that constant.
                                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                                    • Adding a constant to each observation does not change the variance.
                                                                                                                                      • \n\t
                                                                                                                                    • Given the original variance is 8, multiplying each observation by 2 will multiply the variance by The correct answer is 32.

                                                                                                                                      \n\n

                                                                                                                                      Key Points Variance and Data Transformation:

                                                                                                                                      \n\n
                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Variance measures the spread of a set of data points.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • When each observation in a data set is multiplied by a constant, the variance is multiplied by the square of that constant.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Adding a constant to each observation does not change the variance.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Given the original variance is 8, multiplying each observation by 2 will multiply the variance by 22=422=422=4\n\t\n\t .
                                                                                                                                        • \n
                                                                                                                                      \n\n

                                                                                                                                      Important Points

                                                                                                                                      \n\n

                                                                                                                                       Let's calculate the new variance step-by-step:

                                                                                                                                      \n\n
                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Step 1: Original variance = 8.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Step 2: Multiply each observation by 2: New variance = 8×4=328×4=328×4=32\n\t\n\t .
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Step 3: Adding a constant (3) to each observation does not change the variance.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Step 4: The final variance remains 32.
                                                                                                                                        • \n
                                                                                                                                      \n\n

                                                                                                                                      Hence, the variance of the new data set is 32.

                                                                                                                                        Key Points

                                                                                                                                        \n\n
                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                        • Sample Mean:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                            \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                          • The sample mean is the arithmetic average of all sample observations and serves as an unbiased estimator of the population mean.
                                                                                                                                            • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                          • In financial enterprises, it is often used to estimate the average return on investments, average costs, or other financial metrics.

                                                                                                                                          • An unbiased estimator means that the expected value of the sample mean equals the true population mean, making it a reliable measure for decision-making.

                                                                                                                                                    • प्रवृत्ति, आवधिक परिवर्तन और यादृच्छिक या अनियमित गतियाँ:\n\n\t

                                                                                                                                                      • प्रवृत्ति: समय श्रेणी में दीर्घकालिक गति को दर्शाता है। वित्तीय उद्यमों के लिए, यह लंबी अवधि में बाजार की कीमतों, ब्याज दरों या आर्थिक संकेतकों की सामान्य दिशा का संकेत दे सकता है।

                                                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                      • यादृच्छिक या अनियमित गतियाँ: ये अप्रत्याशित उतार-चढ़ाव हैं जो किसी पैटर्न का पालन नहीं करते हैं। ये अचानक बाजार की घटनाओं, भू-राजनीतिक घटनाओं या अप्रत्याशित वित्तीय समाचारों के कारण हो सकते हैं।
                                                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                      • साथ में, ये घटक वित्तीय समय श्रेणी डेटा में अंतर्निहित गतिशीलता की व्यापक समझ प्रदान करते हैं, बेहतर निर्णय लेने और पूर्वानुमान में सहायता करते हैं।

                                                                                                                                                    Key Points

                                                                                                                                                    • Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                        \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                      • This formula is known as the empirical relationship between the mean, median, and mode in a moderately skewed distribution. It is often used in financial analysis to understand the distribution of financial data such as returns or asset prices.
                                                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                      • In a financial enterprise, this relationship helps in identifying the skewness of the data which can be crucial for risk management and investment decisions.
                                                                                                                                                        • \n\t\t
