                                                                                                                                                          Key Points

                                                                                                                                                          \n\n
                                                                                                                                                            \n\t
                                                                                                                                                          • Coefficient of variation:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                              \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • The coefficient of variation (CV) is a relative measure of dispersion that indicates the extent of variability in relation to the mean of the population.
                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • It is calculated as the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean, often expressed as a percentage.
                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • In a financial enterprise, CV is useful for comparing the degree of variation from one data series to another, even if the means are drastically different. This is particularly useful in risk assessment and portfolio management.

                                                                                                                                                          Additional Information

                                                                                                                                                          \n\n
                                                                                                                                                            \n\t
                                                                                                                                                          • Variance:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                              \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • Variance is an absolute measure of dispersion that calculates the average of the squared differences from the mean.
                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • While it gives insights into the data's spread, it does not provide a relative perspective. Hence, it is not suitable for comparing datasets with different units or scales.
                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                            \n\t
                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                          • Range:\n\t
                                                                                                                                                              \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • Range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values in a dataset. It is a simple measure of dispersion but does not consider the distribution of all data points.

                                                                                                                                                            • It is an absolute measure and does not account for the mean or standard deviation, making it less useful for relative comparisons.
                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                            \n\t
                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                          • Mean deviation:\n\t
                                                                                                                                                              \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • Mean deviation, or average absolute deviation, measures the average of the absolute differences between each data point and the mean.
                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • Like variance, it is an absolute measure and does not provide a relative sense of variability, making it less useful for comparing datasets with different scales.

                                                                                                                                                            • प्रसरण गुणांक (CV) प्रकीर्णन का एक सापेक्ष माप है जो जनसंख्या के माध्य के संबंध में परिवर्तनशीलता की सीमा को इंगित करता है।
                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • यह मानक विचलन का माध्य से अनुपात के रूप में गणना की जाती है, जिसे अक्सर प्रतिशत के रूप में व्यक्त किया जाता है।
                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                            • एक वित्तीय उद्यम में, CV एक आंकड़े श्रृंखला से दूसरे में भिन्नता की डिग्री की तुलना करने के लिए उपयोगी है, भले ही माध्य बहुत अलग हों। यह जोखिम मूल्यांकन और पोर्टफोलियो प्रबंधन में विशेष रूप से उपयोगी है।

                                                                                                                                                              • The mean (λ) and the variance of a Poisson distribution are both equal to the same value.

                                                                                                                                                              • The standard deviation of a Poisson distribution is the square root of its mean.

                                                                                                                                                                      \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                    • In a one-way classified data analysis, the total number of degrees of freedom is given by the total number of experimental units minus one (n-1).
                                                                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                    • The degrees of freedom for the treatments are given by the number of treatments minus one (v-1).
                                                                                                                                                                      • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                    • The degrees of freedom for the error term (residuals) are calculated as the total degrees of freedom minus the degrees of freedom for the treatments, which results in (n-1) - (v-1) = n-v.

                                                                                                                                                                      The correct answer is mean = median = mode.

                                                                                                                                                                      Key Points

                                                                                                                                                                      \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                      • For a symmetrical distribution, we have: mean = median = mode:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • In a symmetrical distribution, the left and right sides of the distribution are mirror images of each other.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • This symmetry implies that the central tendency measures (mean, median, and mode) are all located at the center of the distribution and are equal.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • In financial enterprises, such distributions often simplify the analysis of data, as the central point provides a clear and unambiguous measure of central tendency.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • For example, if analyzing the returns of a well-diversified portfolio that follows a normal distribution, the mean, median, and mode of the returns will be the same, providing a clear indication of the expected return.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • \n
                                                                                                                                                                      \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                      Additional Information

                                                                                                                                                                      \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                      • mean > median > mode:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • This relationship typically occurs in a positively skewed distribution, where the tail on the right side is longer than on the left.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • In financial enterprises, this may be observed in income distributions where a small number of high-income individuals skew the mean upwards.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                      • mean < median < mode:\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • This relationship is seen in a negatively skewed distribution, where the tail on the left side is longer than on the right.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • In finance, this could be seen in the distribution of losses where a few large losses pull the mean down below the median and mode.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                      • mean < median = mode:\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • This scenario is uncommon and does not typically represent any standard distribution pattern.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • It could theoretically occur in some specific, non-standard distributions but is not generally applicable in typical financial data analysis.
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        \n\t

                                                                                                                                                                        Key Points

                                                                                                                                                                        \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • Analysis of one-way classified data is used to compare several population means:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                            \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • In financial enterprises, one-way ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) is a statistical method used to compare the means of three or more independent groups to determine if there are any statistically significant differences between the means of the groups.
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • This method is essential for comparing performance metrics, such as average returns of different investment portfolios, average sales figures across different regions, or average operational costs across various departments.
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • By using one-way ANOVA, financial analysts can make informed decisions on resource allocation, investment strategies, and operational improvements based on the comparative analysis of multiple groups.
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n
                                                                                                                                                                        \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                        Additional Information

                                                                                                                                                                        \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • Population standard deviations:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                            \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • This option is incorrect because one-way ANOVA focuses on comparing means, not standard deviations. Standard deviations measure the dispersion or variability within a single dataset.
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • Population variances:\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                            \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • While ANOVA does involve variances in its calculations, its primary purpose is not to compare variances directly but to use them as a means to test the differences between group means.
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • Two population means:\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                            \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • This option is incorrect because the comparison of two population means is typically performed using a t-test, not ANOVA. One-way ANOVA is used when comparing more than two means.

                                                                                                                                                                        सही उत्तर कई जनसंख्या माध्य है।

                                                                                                                                                                        \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                        Key Points 

                                                                                                                                                                        \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • एकतरफा वर्गीकृत आकड़े का विश्लेषण कई जनसंख्या माध्य की तुलना करने के लिए किया जाता है:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                            \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • वित्तीय उद्यमों में, एकतरफा ANOVA (प्रसरण का विश्लेषण) एक सांख्यिकीय विधि है जिसका उपयोग तीन या अधिक स्वतंत्र समूहों के माध्य की तुलना करने के लिए किया जाता है ताकि यह निर्धारित किया जा सके कि समूहों के माध्य के बीच कोई सांख्यिकीय रूप से महत्वपूर्ण अंतर है या नहीं।
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • यह विधि विभिन्न निवेश पोर्टफोलियो के औसत रिटर्न, विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में औसत बिक्री के आंकड़े या विभिन्न विभागों में औसत परिचालन लागत जैसे प्रदर्शन मेट्रिक्स की तुलना करने के लिए आवश्यक है।
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • एकतरफा ANOVA का उपयोग करके, वित्तीय विश्लेषक कई समूहों के तुलनात्मक विश्लेषण के आधार पर संसाधन आवंटन, निवेश रणनीतियों और परिचालन सुधारों पर सूचित निर्णय ले सकते हैं।
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n
                                                                                                                                                                        \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                        Additional Information 

                                                                                                                                                                        \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • जनसंख्या मानक विचलन:\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                            \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • यह विकल्प गलत है क्योंकि एकतरफा ANOVA माध्य की तुलना करने पर केंद्रित है, मानक विचलन पर नहीं। मानक विचलन एकल आकड़े  के भीतर फैलाव या परिवर्तनशीलता को मापता है।
                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                        • जनसंख्या विचरण:\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                            \n\t\t

                                                                                                                                                                              \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                            • A statistic is a numerical measure that describes a characteristic of a sample.                                                                                                                                                                               • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                            • For example, a financial analyst might calculate the average return on a sample of investments to estimate the expected return for a larger portfolio.
                                                                                                                                                                              • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                            • Statistics are crucial for making informed decisions based on sample data, especially when it is impractical to analyze an entire population.

                                                                                                                                                                              Key Points Mean Deviation:

                                                                                                                                                                              \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • Mean deviation measures the average of the absolute deviations of each data point from a central point (mean or median).
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • When a linear transformation is applied to a dataset, the mean deviation is scaled by the absolute value of the coefficient of the variable.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • For the transformation Y = aX + b, the mean deviation of Y from its mean is |a| times the mean deviation of X from its mean.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • The constant term b does not affect the mean deviation as it shifts all values uniformly.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n
                                                                                                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                              Important Points

                                                                                                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • Mean deviation is influenced only by the coefficient of the variable, not the constant term.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • Hence, this option is incorrect.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t

                                                                                                                                                                                • This option ignores the effect of the coefficient a on the mean deviation.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t\t

                                                                                                                                                                              Key Points Sum of Squares Within Groups (SSW):

                                                                                                                                                                              \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • SSW measures the variability within each treatment group.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • It is calculated by summing the squared differences between each observation and its treatment group mean.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • The formula Σkj=1Σnji=1(xij−x¯j)2Σkj=1Σnji=1(xij−x¯j)2Σj=1kΣi=1nj(xij−x¯j)2\n\t\n\t correctly represents this calculation.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • This formula ensures that we capture the variation within each group and not between groups.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n
                                                                                                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                              Important Points

                                                                                                                                                                              \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                                \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • Option 2: Σkj=1nj(x¯j−x¯)2Σkj=1nj(x¯j−x¯)2Σj=1knj(x¯j−x¯)2\n\t\n\t calculates the Sum of Squares Between Groups (SSB), not within groups.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                              • Option 3: Σkj=1(x¯j−x¯)Σkj=1(x¯j−x¯)Σj=1k(x¯j−x¯)\n\t\n\t is incorrect as it does not involve squaring the differences or considering all observations.
                                                                                                                                                                                • \n\t

                                                                                                                                                                                • \n
                                                                                                                                                                              \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                              Hence, the correct formula for calculating the sum of squares within groups (SSW) is Σkj=1Σnji=1(xij−x¯j)2Σkj=1Σnji=1(xij−x¯j)2Σj=1kΣi=1nj(xij−x¯j)2\n\n .

                                                                                                                                                                                Key Points Degrees of Freedom in Randomised Block Design:

                                                                                                                                                                                \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • In a randomised block design, we have 't' treatments and 'r' replicates, leading to a total of 'rt' observations.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • The total degrees of freedom (DF) for the sum of squares is given by the total number of observations minus 1.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • This results in the formula: DF = rt - 1.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • Therefore, the correct answer is option 4, which is 'rt - 1'.

                                                                                                                                                                                The correct answer is The correct answer is Sum of squares due to treatmentsv−1Sum of squares due to treatmentsv−1\n\n

                                                                                                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                                Key Points Mean Sum of Squares due to Treatments:

                                                                                                                                                                                \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • Sum of Squares due to Treatments (SST) is the total variation explained by the treatments in the experiment.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • The degrees of freedom for treatments is v−1v−1\n\t\n\t, where vv\n\t\n\tis the number of treatments.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • The Mean Sum of Squares due to Treatments (MST) is calculated as SSTv−1SSTv−1\n\t\n\t.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • This measure helps to determine if the differences between treatments are statistically significant.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n
                                                                                                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                                Important Points

                                                                                                                                                                                \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                                 Let's examine why the other options are incorrect:

                                                                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The denominator n−vn−v\n\t\t\n\t\tdoes not represent the correct degrees of freedom for treatments.
                                                                                                                                                                                    • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • It incorrectly suggests that the total number of experimental units affects the calculation of MST.

                                                                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t

                                                                                                                                                                                  \n\tIncorrect because:\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The formula for Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is: r_s = 1 - (6 Σ d²) / (n(n² - 1)), where d is the difference in ranks of each pair of values and n is the total number of values being compared.
                                                                                                                                                                                    • \n\t\t

                                                                                                                                                                                  \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • SPEARMAN'S RANK CORRELATION COEFFICIENT\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The formula for Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is: r_s = 1 - (6 Σ d²) / (n(n² - 1)), where d is the difference in ranks of each pair of values and n is the total number of values being compared.
                                                                                                                                                                                    • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The value of r_s ranges from -1 to +1, indicating perfect negative and positive correlation respectively.
                                                                                                                                                                                    • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The maximum value of the sum of squared differences (∑d²) in the formula occurs when the ranks are as different as possible, i.e., in a situation of complete disagreement between the ranks.

                                                                                                                                                                                Additional Information

                                                                                                                                                                                • Calculation of Maximum Value of ∑d²\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The maximum value of ∑d² occurs when the ranks are completely reversed, i.e., the largest value is assigned the smallest rank, and the smallest value is assigned the largest rank.
                                                                                                                                                                                    • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • This results in the maximum possible difference between ranks, thereby leading to the maximum value for ∑d² in the numerator.
                                                                                                                                                                                    • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The correct formula is 1/3 n(n² - 1), which corresponds to the scenario where the ranks are as far apart as possible.

                                                                                                                                                                                  • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                • Rank Correlation Formula Application\n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                    \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is widely used in cases where the data does not follow a normal distribution and when the relationship between variables is not linear.
                                                                                                                                                                                    • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The formula applies to both tied and untied ranks, though the maximum value of ∑d² for untied ranks is specific and results in the answer shown in option 4.

                                                                                                                                                                                प्रमुख बिंदु

                                                                                                                                                                                  • स्पीयरमैन के रैंक सहसंबंध गुणांक का सूत्र है: r_s = 1 - (6 Σ d²) / (n(n² - 1)) , जहां d मानों के प्रत्येक जोड़े के रैंक में अंतर है और n तुलना किए जा रहे मानों की कुल संख्या है।
                                                                                                                                                                                  • r_s का मान -1 से +1 तक होता है, जो क्रमशः पूर्ण नकारात्मक और सकारात्मक सहसंबंध को दर्शाता है।
                                                                                                                                                                                  • सूत्र में वर्ग अंतरों के योग (∑d²) का अधिकतम मान तब होता है जब रैंक यथासंभव भिन्न होते हैं, अर्थात, रैंकों के बीच पूर्ण असहमति की स्थिति में।

                                                                                                                                                                                अतिरिक्त जानकारी

                                                                                                                                                                                • ∑d² के अधिकतम मान की गणना
                                                                                                                                                                                  • ∑d² का अधिकतम मान तब होता है जब रैंक पूरी तरह से उलट दी जाती है, अर्थात, सबसे बड़े मान को सबसे छोटा रैंक दिया जाता है, और सबसे छोटे मान को सबसे बड़ा रैंक दिया जाता है।
                                                                                                                                                                                  • इसके परिणामस्वरूप रैंकों के बीच अधिकतम संभव अंतर होता है, जिससे अंश में ∑d² का अधिकतम मान प्राप्त होता है।
                                                                                                                                                                                  • सही सूत्र 1/3 n(n² - 1) है, जो उस परिदृश्य से मेल खाता है जहां रैंक यथासंभव दूर हैं।
                                                                                                                                                                                • रैंक सहसंबंध सूत्र अनुप्रयोग
                                                                                                                                                                                  • स्पीयरमैन रैंक सहसंबंध गुणांक का उपयोग व्यापक रूप से उन मामलों में किया जाता है जहां डेटा सामान्य वितरण का पालन नहीं करता है और जब चरों के बीच संबंध रैखिक नहीं होता है।
                                                                                                                                                                                  • सूत्र बंधे और अनबंधे दोनों रैंकों पर लागू होता है, हालांकि अनबंधे रैंकों के लिए ∑d² का अधिकतम मान विशिष्ट है और इसका परिणाम विकल्प 4 में दिखाए गए उत्तर में होता है।

                                                                                                                                                                                          Key Points Median Calculation:

                                                                                                                                                                                          \n\n
                                                                                                                                                                                            \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                          • Median is the middle value in a data set when arranged in ascending order.
                                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                          • For a data set with an even number of observations, the median is the average of the two middle numbers.
                                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                          • With 24 observations, the median is the average of the 12th and 13th values.
                                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                          • In the given data set, the 12th value is 29 and the 13th value is 30.
                                                                                                                                                                                            • \n\t
                                                                                                                                                                                          • Therefore, the median is (29 + 30) / 2 = 29.5.
                                                                                                                                                                                            • \n
                                                                                                                                                                                          \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                                          \n\n

                                                                                                                                                                                          Hence, the correct answer is 29.5.
